key_insight: A mixed discrete Cosserat rod model can be derived rigorously from a low-order mixed Petrov–Galerkin FEM, yielding a two-node rigid-body chain with compliant inter-node forces and moments.
engineering_relevance: This gives a robust, lock-free rod discretization that is attractive for soft robotics and other slender-structure simulations needing efficient coupling between kinematics and internal forces.
method: Represent the rod as rigid nodes connected by elastic interactions between adjacent pairs
Compute dilatation, shear, torsion, and curvature from relative node kinematics
Use compliance-form constitutive laws with independent stress degrees of freedom; midpoint/trapezoidal quadrature recovers the mixed FEM structure
evidence_signal: Three numerical examples—varying cross sections, tendon-driven actuation, and coupled longitudinal-torsional dynamics—show accuracy, robustness, and convergence.
watch_item: The method depends on consistent midpoint/trapezoidal integration and careful handling of pairwise couplings to preserve the mixed FEM benefits.
paper_title: A Mixed Discrete Cosserat Rod Formulation
